newsitem.title: USA: Group says energy efficiency could cut LILCO rates.
newsitem.headline: Group says energy efficiency could cut LILCO rates.

text.p: The National Resources Defense Council (NRDC) said Monday energy efficiency is an effective way to help bring down the sky-high electric rates of Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO) customers.

In a presentation before the Long Island Power Agency (LIPA), NRDC senior economist Ashok Gupta said efforts toward energy conservation alone could bring the double digit rate reduction desired by LIPA and LILCO consumers.
Citing a recent LILCO study, Gupta said LILCO could achieve $400 million in savings if it slashes power usage by 17.8 percent, or 3,437 gigawatt hours, by the year 2000.
Energy efficiency would augment the cost savings in any rate reduction being examined by LIPA, Gupta added.
LIPA, a state agency, has been studying a refinancing proposal to acquire mothballed Shoreham nuclear power plant and debt associated with the project.

On December 29, LILCO and Brooklyn Union Gas Co agreed to merge in a stock transaction that would result in a $4 billion electric and gas company serving 2.2 million customers. The combination would bring $1 billion in savings over 10 years or about a 10 percent rate cut for LILCO consumers.
Gupta said considerable startup costs were needed to tap into energy efficiency as a source for rate reduction.
"It is taking money now and investing it over 10 years," he said, adding it will take an annual investment of $32 million over the first five years.

The money from government and the two utilities for upgrade and investment in energy efficency includes advances to large industrial customers, loan guarantees to small consumers and coupons/rebates to bring energy efficient products into the market, Gupta said.
NRDC is an environmental advocacy group based in New York City.
